Most Likely Diagnosis: Psoriatic Arthritis

Two Recommended Diagnostic Tests:

1. Rheumatoid Factor (RF) and Anti-Cyclic Citrullinated Peptide (anti-CCP) antibodies
2. X-rays of affected joints (knees and any other symptomatic joints)

Reasoning:
The patient presents with established psoriasis and is receiving knee injections for joint symptoms, combined with the characteristic distribution of skin lesions including palmoplantar involvement (palms and soles). This clinical presentation strongly suggests psoriatic arthritis. 

- RF and anti-CCP testing helps differentiate psoriatic arthritis (typically seronegative) from rheumatoid arthritis (often seropositive)
- Joint imaging (X-rays) can reveal characteristic changes of psoriatic arthritis such as joint space narrowing, erosions, and new bone formation

2. Emphasize the importance of early treatment to prevent joint damage and disability

4. Review treatment options which may include:
   - Disease-modifying antirheumatic drugs (DMARDs) like methotrexate
   - Biologic therapies that can treat both skin and joint symptoms
   - Continued orthopedic care for joint management as needed
5. Stress the importance of regular monitoring and follow-up
